title: Convergence Checker: API + Model Smokeburst for Private Deploys
creator: Amina Patel
description: Add a lightweight, idempotent "smokeburst" harness that runs as a post-deploy job for private (VPC) deployments to validate API readiness and model load correctness after Terraform-driven provisioning and runtime upgrades. The harness should be runnable from CI, from a customer-facing operator console job, or triggered by Terraform via a null_resource local-exec hook. It needs to exercise a short, representative set of model invocations at ramped concurrency, validate KV-cache attach/restore behavior, and exercise standard API surface (auth handshake, streaming, and function call frame).
goal: Provide an automated, low-cost post-deploy verification that detects regressions in (1) API handshake and auth, (2) model instantiate/load failures, (3) extreme latency or early OOMs during load ramp, and (4) observable discrepancy vs golden outputs. Fail fast and provide actionable logs/links for oncall and devs.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable CLI job + container image added to infra repo that can be invoked by CI and Terraform hooks
The job performs: auth handshake, a streaming generation check, a 3-step concurrency ramp (1->4->8), and a KV-cache priming/restore probe
Failures are translated into clearly typed exit codes (auth, model-load, performance, mismatch) and uploaded artifacts to S3/obj store
A Grafana dashboard and a short Playbook link are published summarizing how to interpret failures
Run completes within 7 minutes by default and consumes bounded GPU cycles (configurable via env vars)
Integration tests added that exercise the harness in a lightweight local emulator and in the real private stage cluster
implementation_plan: Design: define 'smokeburst' scenario set and output golden traces (constrained tokens, deterministic seed) - Amina
Infra: build a minimal Docker container with Redwood CLI test harness + python runner; publish to internal registry - Diego
Terraform integration: add optional null_resource 'post_deploy_smokeburst' that can call the container image; keep disabled by default and gated by a boolean variable
Runtime hooks: make the harness call health endpoints first (auth token fetch, /healthz), then warm KV cache by a short prefix run, then run ramped concurrency generation checks
Observability: emit structured logs to S3 and push a single Prometheus metric 'smokeburst_last_status' and duration histogram
Release: land infra PR, smoke runner PR, and console-runbook; schedule a canary run against dev-private cluster prior to enabling on customer rollouts
tradeoffs_and_notes: We debated embedding the check into Terraform vs running from an external orchestration lambdas; embedding keeps a simpler operator flow but risks long Terraform apply times - decided to keep it opt-in and short to avoid blocking applies
Using deterministic golden outputs reduces flakiness but requires pinning model revisions for the check; we will use model-version variables and allow a loose 'fuzzy-match' mode for model families
KV-cache attach/restore is non-deterministic across runtime versions; the harness will capture timing windows and mark warnings versus hard failures
We intentionally limit concurrency ramp to modest sizes to avoid heavy cost during CI runs; a separate 'stress' job lives in a different ticket
risks: False negatives if the golden set doesn't exercise a failing code path
Terraform apply timeouts if customers inadvertently enable the check on slow control planes
Potential leakage of secrets if teardown isn't robust; ensure token lifetimes and short lived creds
